quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Amara gets up early on school days. She packs her bag, eats rice and eggs, and catches the bus at seven. By half past seven, she is sitting at her desk.
options: Amara is often late for the school bus in the mornings.
Amara gets ready and travels to school in the morning.
Amara studies quietly at her desk after school ends.
Amara eats rice and eggs for breakfast before she leaves home.
quests.correctAnswer: Amara gets ready and travels to school in the morning.
quests.hint: Ask what the whole paragraph is about, not what happens in just one sentence.
quests.explanation: The paragraph follows Amara from waking up to sitting at her desk, so the main idea is her whole morning journey to school. Breakfast is only one small step inside that routine.
keyPoints: Amara has a regular morning routine on school days.
She packs her bag, eats breakfast and takes the bus.
The routine gets her to her desk by half past seven.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Biscuit is a small brown dog. Every afternoon he waits by the door for the children to come home from school. When they arrive, he jumps up and wags his tail.
options: Biscuit waits by the door because he wants his dinner.
The children take Biscuit for a long walk every afternoon.
A dog is always excited to greet the children after school.
Biscuit is a small brown dog who likes to sit by the door.
quests.correctAnswer: A dog is always excited to greet the children after school.
quests.hint: Some options describe one true detail. Look for the idea that the sentences share.
quests.explanation: Each sentence shows the dog's daily welcome: waiting, then jumping and wagging when the children arrive. The colour and size of the dog are just description, not the main point.
keyPoints: Biscuit is a family dog who waits for the children each afternoon.
He waits by the door until they come home from school.
When they arrive, he jumps up and wags his tail happily.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: On Sundays, Mr. Osei makes soup for his family. He cuts carrots and onions while the water boils. Everyone sits down to eat at one o'clock.
options: Mr. Osei cooks Sunday soup for his family.
Mr. Osei is teaching his children how to make soup.
On Sundays, the Osei family eats out at a restaurant.
Mr. Osei carefully cuts carrots and onions in the kitchen.
quests.correctAnswer: Mr. Osei cooks Sunday soup for his family.
quests.hint: Picture the paragraph from start to finish. What is the whole activity?
quests.explanation: The paragraph shows a Sunday habit: Mr. Osei cooks soup and the family eats together. Cutting vegetables is just one step in that larger activity.
keyPoints: Mr. Osei cooks soup for his family on Sundays.
He cuts the vegetables while the water boils.
The whole family sits down to eat together at one o'clock.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The market near Kenji's home opens at eight. Farmers bring fresh fruit, vegetables and flowers in their trucks. By nine, many neighbours are already shopping.
options: Farmers drive their trucks into the city every day.
Kenji sells flowers to shoppers at the market.
Neighbours shop at a busy morning market.
The market closes at nine each morning.
quests.correctAnswer: Neighbours shop at a busy morning market.
quests.hint: Pay attention to who is in the paragraph and what they are all doing together.
quests.explanation: Farmers bring goods and neighbours arrive to buy them, which makes the market itself the central idea. The trucks and flowers are supporting details.
keyPoints: A local market opens early in the morning.
Farmers bring fresh fruit, vegetables and flowers by truck.
By nine o'clock, many neighbours are already shopping there.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The town library has a quiet room for studying. Students go there after school to do their homework. The librarian keeps the room calm and tidy.
options: The librarian works at the town library all day long.
Students borrow the most books after school each day.
The library is closed to students in the afternoon.
The library's quiet room helps students study.
quests.correctAnswer: The library's quiet room helps students study.
quests.hint: Cross out options that mention only one person or one action from the paragraph.
quests.explanation: The room, the students and the librarian all connect to one idea: a calm place where students can study. An option about the librarian alone leaves out why the room matters.
keyPoints: The library has a quiet room made for studying.
Students use it after school to do homework.
The librarian keeps the room calm and tidy.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Bus 12 goes from the train station to the hospital. It stops at the park and the post office on the way. Buses run every ten minutes.
options: The hospital is building a brand-new bus station.
Bus 12 links several useful places and runs often.
Bus 12 stops at the town park and the post office.
Bus 12 only runs in the evening, every ten minutes.
quests.correctAnswer: Bus 12 links several useful places and runs often.
quests.hint: Which option covers the route, the stops and how often the bus comes?
quests.explanation: The paragraph describes a route linking the station, park, post office and hospital, plus how frequently it runs. The park stop is only one piece of that route.
keyPoints: Bus 12 is a route that links important places in town.
It goes from the train station to the hospital.
It stops at the park and post office, and a bus comes every ten minutes.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ravi is wearing a warm coat and boots today. Snow fell all night, and the streets are white and slippery. He walks slowly to the bus stop.
options: Ravi misses his bus because the snow is so heavy.
Ravi buys a new warm coat and boots for the winter.
The streets in Ravi's town are white and slippery.
Ravi dresses warmly and walks carefully because of the snow.
quests.correctAnswer: Ravi dresses warmly and walks carefully because of the snow.
quests.hint: Think about why Ravi does each thing. What single reason connects them?
quests.explanation: The snow explains both his warm clothes and his slow walk. The paragraph is about how Ravi responds to the weather, not about one item he is wearing.
keyPoints: Snow has covered the streets overnight.
Ravi wears a warm coat and boots in response.
He walks slowly to the bus stop because the ground is slippery.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Leila's phone stopped working this morning. She took it to a repair shop near her school. The worker fixed it in one hour, and Leila went home happy.
options: Leila's phone suddenly stopped working this morning.
Leila got her broken phone repaired at a nearby shop.
A repair worker gives a phone lesson at Leila's school.
Leila buys a new phone at a shop near her school.
quests.correctAnswer: Leila got her broken phone repaired at a nearby shop.
quests.hint: A good summary usually covers how a paragraph begins and how it ends.
quests.explanation: The paragraph gives a problem, a repair shop, and a solved problem. Saying only that the phone stopped working leaves out what Leila did about it.
keyPoints: Leila's phone suddenly stopped working this morning.
She took it to a repair shop near her school.
The phone was fixed in an hour, so she went home happy.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ines waters her plants every evening. Her tomatoes need a lot of water, but her flowers need only a little. She checks each one before going inside.
options: Tomatoes need much more water than flowers do.
Ines grows tomatoes in her garden to sell at the market.
Ines looks after her plants every evening.
Ines is planting a brand-new garden this week.
quests.correctAnswer: Ines looks after her plants every evening.
quests.hint: Ask yourself: is this option about the whole habit, or about one comparison inside it?
quests.explanation: Ines has a regular habit of looking after her plants, and the water needs of tomatoes and flowers are examples of how careful she is. The comparison is a detail, not the whole paragraph.
keyPoints: Ines has an evening habit of watering her plants.
She gives each kind of plant the amount of water it needs.
She checks every plant before she goes inside.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Nadia is saving money every week. She puts five dollars in a jar and does not buy snacks at school. She wants a new bicycle for her birthday.
options: Nadia puts five dollars in a jar every week.
Nadia sells snacks at school to pay for a bicycle.
Nadia gives her school snacks to hungry classmates.
Nadia saves her money because she wants a bicycle.
quests.correctAnswer: Nadia saves her money because she wants a bicycle.
quests.hint: Look for the reason behind Nadia's actions, not only the actions themselves.
quests.explanation: The paragraph explains what Nadia does and why she does it. Because the bicycle gives the purpose, it must be part of a strong summary.
keyPoints: Nadia is saving money every week.
She puts money in a jar and skips buying snacks.
Her goal is to get a new bicycle for her birthday.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The school has put a recycling box in every classroom. Students put paper and plastic bottles inside. The class with the fullest box wins a small prize.
options: Every classroom receives a brand-new box each week.
A school encourages recycling through a class competition.
Students in the school recycle only plastic bottles and cans.
Students win small prizes for cleaning the playground.
quests.correctAnswer: A school encourages recycling through a class competition.
quests.hint: Find the idea that ties the boxes, the students and the prize together.
quests.explanation: The boxes, the items collected and the prize all support one plan: getting students to recycle. The prize is part of that plan, but the plan itself is the main idea.
keyPoints: The school has started a recycling programme.
Each classroom has a box for paper and plastic bottles.
The class with the fullest box gets a small prize.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Emeka takes the stairs instead of the elevator at work. His office is on the sixth floor, so it is good exercise. He feels stronger and has more energy.
options: The elevator in Emeka's office building is often broken.
Emeka's office is on the sixth floor of a tall building.
Emeka takes the stairs at work to stay healthy.
Emeka goes to the gym before he starts work each day.
quests.correctAnswer: Emeka takes the stairs at work to stay healthy.
quests.hint: Notice the choice, the reason for it, and the result. Which option holds all three?
quests.explanation: The paragraph links a choice (stairs), a reason (exercise) and a result (more energy). The floor number is a fact that only supports the story.
keyPoints: Emeka chooses the stairs instead of the elevator.
Climbing six floors gives him regular exercise.
As a result, he feels stronger and has more energy.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The Rossi family had a picnic by the lake on Sunday. Grandpa brought sandwiches, and the children played football on the grass. Everyone stayed until the sun went down.
options: The children played a football match at a big stadium.
Grandpa brought sandwiches for the whole family to share.
A family spent Sunday enjoying a picnic by the lake.
Grandpa spent the whole day fishing at the lake.
quests.correctAnswer: A family spent Sunday enjoying a picnic by the lake.
quests.hint: When a paragraph describes an event, ask what the event was, not what one person did.
quests.explanation: Grandpa, the children and the lake are all parts of one family picnic. A summary about only Grandpa's sandwiches would miss the event as a whole.
keyPoints: The Rossi family had a picnic at the lake on Sunday.
Grandpa brought food and the children played football.
They all stayed until sunset.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ms. Petrov's class held a bake sale on Friday. Students brought cookies and cakes from home and sold them in the hallway. They raised money for new books.
options: A class sold baked goods to raise money for books.
Students brought cakes and cookies from home on Friday.
Ms. Petrov sold cakes to pay for a new car.
Students learned to bake cakes in Ms. Petrov's class.
quests.correctAnswer: A class sold baked goods to raise money for books.
quests.hint: Who did what, and what was the goal? A good summary answers both questions.
quests.explanation: The class sold food, and the reason was to raise money for books. Saying only that students brought cakes leaves out the purpose that makes the event meaningful.
keyPoints: Ms. Petrov's class held a bake sale on Friday.
Students sold cookies and cakes they brought from home.
The money they raised will buy new books.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: There was a small concert in the park on Saturday. A local band played for two hours while people sat on blankets. Many families stayed to listen.
options: A famous band played a concert at a big school.
People sat on blankets on the grass in the park.
The park closed early because of heavy rain.
Families listened to a local band play in the park.
quests.correctAnswer: Families listened to a local band play in the park.
quests.hint: Look for the option that describes the whole event instead of one small scene.
quests.explanation: The paragraph is about a concert and the people who came to hear it. The blankets are only a small detail about how the audience was sitting.
keyPoints: A concert took place in the park on Saturday.
A local band played for two hours.
Many families sat on blankets and stayed to listen.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Yuki loves drawing. She draws animals in her notebook on the train, and she sketches her friends at lunch. On weekends, she paints bigger pictures at home.
options: Yuki paints large pictures to sell online on weekends.
Yuki draws only pictures of her friends at lunch.
Yuki goes to an art class every weekend afternoon.
Yuki enjoys drawing and does it in many places.
quests.correctAnswer: Yuki enjoys drawing and does it in many places.
quests.hint: Which idea appears again and again, even though the places change?
quests.explanation: The train, the lunch table and home are different places, but Yuki is doing the same thing in all of them. The repeated idea is her love of drawing.
keyPoints: Yuki has a strong love of drawing.
She draws on the train, at lunch and at home.
On weekends, she makes larger paintings.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Mateo runs before breakfast three days a week. On Tuesdays he runs with a neighbour, and on Saturdays he joins a local running club. He says running helps him feel calm.
options: Mateo eats breakfast with his neighbour every day.
Mateo runs often because it helps him feel calm.
Mateo runs only on Saturdays with a group of people.
Mateo joins a local running club so that he can win races.
quests.correctAnswer: Mateo runs often because it helps him feel calm.
quests.hint: Separate the reason from the schedule. What does Mateo get from all these runs?
quests.explanation: The days and running partners show how often and with whom he runs, but the paragraph ends on what running does for him. A good summary joins the habit with its benefit.
keyPoints: Mateo runs three mornings a week.
Sometimes he runs with a neighbour or a club.
He says running makes him feel calm.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Kofi practises the guitar every evening after dinner. He learns new songs from videos. Before bed, he plays for his little sister, and she always asks for one more.
options: Kofi enjoys practising the guitar and playing for his sister.
Kofi plays the guitar in a school band with friends.
Kofi's little sister is learning how to play the guitar too.
Kofi learns new songs by watching guitar videos every evening.
quests.correctAnswer: Kofi enjoys practising the guitar and playing for his sister.
quests.hint: Think about how the paragraph ends. Does your choice include that ending?
quests.explanation: Kofi's practice leads to playing for his sister, so the paragraph is about both practising and sharing. Learning from videos is only one way he practises.
keyPoints: Kofi practises the guitar every evening.
He learns new songs from videos.
He plays for his little sister, who always wants more.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Elena is making a list before she goes to the supermarket. She checks the fridge and writes down milk, eggs and rice. This way, she will not forget anything.
options: Elena forgets her list and leaves it at the supermarket.
Elena buys milk, eggs and rice for a birthday party.
Elena makes a list so she will not forget anything.
Elena's fridge is empty, so she rushes out to shop.
quests.correctAnswer: Elena makes a list so she will not forget anything.
quests.hint: The last sentence often gives the reason behind an action. Did your choice use it?
quests.explanation: The paragraph explains an action (writing a list) and its purpose (not forgetting anything). The specific foods are examples of what goes on the list.
keyPoints: Elena makes a list before shopping.
She checks the fridge and writes down what she needs.
The list helps her remember everything at the supermarket.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A sign at the swimming pool says children must wear a swim cap. Adults can choose to wear one, but everyone must shower first. These rules keep the water clean.
options: All adults at the pool must wear a swim cap.
The pool has rules that keep its water clean.
The pool staff clean all the showers every morning.
Children cannot swim in the pool without an adult.
quests.correctAnswer: The pool has rules that keep its water clean.
quests.hint: Watch for options that change a small word, like 'can' or 'must'. Check them against the paragraph.
quests.explanation: The rules about caps and showers all serve one purpose: clean water. One wrong option turns an adult's choice into a requirement, which the paragraph does not say.
keyPoints: The swimming pool has rules for visitors.
Children need swim caps, and everyone must shower first.
The rules exist to keep the water clean.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Mr. Silva is learning to use a tablet. His granddaughter shows him how to send messages and take photos. He practises a little every day so he can talk to his family far away.
options: Mr. Silva is learning how to take good photos with it.
Mr. Silva's granddaughter wants a tablet of her own too.
Mr. Silva takes his tablet on a trip to see his family.
Mr. Silva learns tablet skills to stay in touch with family.
quests.correctAnswer: Mr. Silva learns tablet skills to stay in touch with family.
quests.hint: Look for the person's goal. It usually explains why the small actions matter.
quests.explanation: Sending messages and taking photos are the skills; talking with faraway family is the goal. The best summary joins the learning with the reason for it.
keyPoints: Mr. Silva is learning to use a tablet.
His granddaughter teaches him messaging and photos.
He practises daily so he can stay in touch with far-away family.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: It rained heavily during the football match. The field became muddy, and the players kept slipping. In the end, the referee stopped the game and sent everyone home.
options: The football field was closed for repairs last week.
Heavy rain made a football match end early.
The referee changed the rules during the rainy match.
The players kept slipping on the muddy field.
quests.correctAnswer: Heavy rain made a football match end early.
quests.hint: Follow the chain: what started the trouble, and what did it lead to?
quests.explanation: Rain caused the mud, the mud caused the slipping, and the slipping led to the game stopping. The slipping is a middle step, not the outcome.
keyPoints: Heavy rain fell during a football match.
The mud made the players slip.
The referee finally stopped the game.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Lucas forgot his umbrella and got wet on the way to work. At the office, he hung his coat near the heater and drank hot tea. By lunchtime, he felt warm and dry again.
options: Lucas bought a new umbrella when he got to work.
Lucas warmed up by drinking hot tea at the office.
Lucas caught a bad cold after walking in the rain.
Lucas got wet in the rain but warmed up at work.
quests.correctAnswer: Lucas got wet in the rain but warmed up at work.
quests.hint: Good summaries often show a problem and how it ended. Check that yours does both.
quests.explanation: The paragraph begins with Lucas getting wet and ends with him feeling warm and dry. The tea is only one thing he did to solve the problem.
keyPoints: Lucas got wet because he forgot his umbrella.
At the office, he used the heater and hot tea to warm up.
By lunchtime, he felt warm and dry.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The power went out on the whole street last night. Neighbours lit candles and sat outside to talk. When the lights came back at ten, everyone said goodnight.
options: During a power cut, neighbours spent the evening talking outside.
The lights came back on at ten o'clock that night.
A storm damaged several houses on the street.
Neighbours lit candles to save electricity in the street.
quests.correctAnswer: During a power cut, neighbours spent the evening talking outside.
quests.hint: Decide what the paragraph is mostly about: the event, the people, or the time.
quests.explanation: The power cut is the situation, and the neighbours' conversation is what the paragraph shows happening. The time the lights returned is a small detail.
keyPoints: The power went out on the whole street.
Neighbours lit candles and talked outside together.
Everyone went home when the lights returned at ten.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Dr. Chen works at a small clinic. She sees about twenty patients each day and listens carefully to each one. After the last patient leaves, she writes her notes.
options: Dr. Chen is opening a new clinic near her home.
Dr. Chen spends a busy day seeing her patients.
Dr. Chen sees exactly twenty patients on every working day.
Dr. Chen teaches other doctors how to write good notes.
quests.correctAnswer: Dr. Chen spends a busy day seeing her patients.
quests.hint: A number in a paragraph is usually a detail. Decide what it is a detail of.
quests.explanation: The twenty patients, the careful listening and the final notes all describe one working day. An option about the exact number turns an approximate detail into the main point.
keyPoints: Dr. Chen works at a small clinic.
She sees around twenty patients and listens closely to each.
She finishes the day by writing her notes.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Sipho delivers packages by motorbike. He starts at eight, checks his list, and rides to a different street each hour. Customers often thank him with a smile.
options: Sipho repairs motorbikes every morning before eight o'clock.
Sipho delivers packages to only one street each day.
Customers give Sipho small gifts for his good service.
Sipho's job is riding around delivering packages to customers.
quests.correctAnswer: Sipho's job is riding around delivering packages to customers.
quests.hint: Ask what the person's job is, then see which option describes it best.
quests.explanation: Every sentence describes part of Sipho's delivery work: his schedule, his routes and the customers. The smiles are a pleasant detail, not the central idea.
keyPoints: Sipho delivers packages by motorbike.
He follows a list and visits a different street each hour.
Customers often thank him with a smile.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Mrs. Dube sells vegetables at a market stall. She picks them from her own farm at dawn and arranges them by colour. People enjoy buying from her because everything is fresh.
options: Mrs. Dube sells fresh vegetables from her own farm.
Mrs. Dube has the biggest stall in the market.
Mrs. Dube buys vegetables from other farms every day.
Mrs. Dube arranges her vegetables by colour.
quests.correctAnswer: Mrs. Dube sells fresh vegetables from her own farm.
quests.hint: Which option explains both what she sells and why customers like it?
quests.explanation: Picking at dawn, arranging the stall and pleasing customers all connect to selling fresh vegetables. The colour arrangement is an interesting detail but not the point.
keyPoints: Mrs. Dube runs a vegetable stall at the market.
She picks the vegetables from her own farm at dawn.
Customers like buying from her because everything is fresh.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Anh uses a language app every morning on the bus. It gives her a short lesson and a small quiz. She now knows enough English to order food in a café.
options: Anh quizzes her friends on the bus every morning.
Anh practises English daily with an app and is making progress.
Anh takes a quiz to get a job at a café.
The app teaches only the words that people use for food.
quests.correctAnswer: Anh practises English daily with an app and is making progress.
quests.hint: Look for what she does regularly and what has changed because of it.
quests.explanation: Regular practice on the bus led to a real ability: ordering in English. A summary that only names the app or the quiz misses that progress.
keyPoints: Anh studies English with an app every morning.
Each session has a short lesson and a small quiz.
Her English is now good enough to order in a café.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A neighbourhood group cleans the beach on the first Sunday of each month. Volunteers bring gloves and bags to collect rubbish. The beach looks much better, and more people come to help each time.
options: Volunteers bring gloves and bags to the beach.
The beach is closed on the first Sunday of every month.
Volunteers are paid to collect rubbish from the beach.
Volunteers regularly clean a beach, and their group is growing.
quests.correctAnswer: Volunteers regularly clean a beach, and their group is growing.
quests.hint: Skip the objects mentioned and ask what result the volunteers are getting.
quests.explanation: The paragraph describes a regular activity and its good results: a cleaner beach and more helpers. Gloves and bags are supplies, so they are minor details.
keyPoints: A neighbourhood group cleans the beach every month.
Volunteers use gloves and bags to collect rubbish.
The beach looks better and more people join each time.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Riverside School wants students to drink more water. New water stations have been placed near the gym and the cafeteria. Teachers say water helps students think more clearly in class.
options: Water stations are found only near the school gym.
Teachers ask students to stop using the cafeteria.
The school encourages students to drink more water.
Students think more clearly right after gym class.
quests.correctAnswer: The school encourages students to drink more water.
quests.hint: Check the scope of each option. Does it say more or less than the paragraph does?
quests.explanation: The school has a goal, a new way to reach it and a reason for it. One option limits the stations to the gym, which shrinks the paragraph's information.
keyPoints: The school wants students to drink more water.
It has added water stations near the gym and cafeteria.
Teachers say water helps students think more clearly.
